title: [finding] data errors: the unknown-object heuristic classifies a bare ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED as 404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As5bdhV5T4N9vpjmZzH

## Finding

`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts` — the `looksLikeUnknownObject` heuristic (around line 2045 on main) answers an error whose message carries a bare `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED` (readonly-field rejection that quotes the object name and contains "not") as **404 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`** ("Object 'X' is not registered"), instead of the readonly rejection it is.

Measured in #36259's dev report (comment 7099512890); L1-a's review of #36683 flagged it as worth its own card.

## Reach

No public reach after #36683 lands: no public data door passes `strictReadonlyWrites` any more, so the bare code no longer reaches this classifier from a public route. It is a latent mis-classification for any future/internal caller that re-enables strict readonly writes.

## Expected

A readonly-field rejection is classified by its code (the existing 4xx readonly answer), never by the unknown-object substring heuristic. Same class as #22868 / #5462 (unknown-object heuristic over-matching).

## Acceptance

- A unit test feeding `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED` (with the object name quoted in the message) gets the readonly answer, not 404.
- No change to the 404 answer for genuine unknown objects.

Filed from seat review (repo:objectstack#7).
